title: Wendell and the Border
premise: Dominic Yarrow, a private security contractor who has spent a decade guarding clients nobody trusts, discovers the safe house protecting his latest client—a whistleblower holding proof that a joint intelligence program sells access to assassins—has been listed for sale online, its interior photographed down to the hidden server room. The listing is a message: someone inside the program has sold them out, and the assassin known only as Vesper is already en route. Dominic and the client, Mara Vance, must smuggle the evidence across three borders while deciding whether to trust each other or their handlers. In the end, Dominic chooses love over duty, burning his polished lie and releasing the files publicly at the cost of his own cover, while Vesper—revealed to be another contractor who once loved him—lets them walk away rather than finish the job.
about_author: Xanthe Galloway is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator for international security firms who writes thrillers drawn from the moral gray zones she witnessed firsthand. She lives off-grid in coastal Wales with her partner and an aging boat named after a debt she never repaid.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet him mid-routine: checking sightlines at a Rotterdam safe house, rehearsing his cover story about being a property manager, keeping his go-bag by the door. His client, Mara Vance, is paranoid, brilliant, and slowly dismantling his emotional armor. The beat: comfort before catastrophe—the calm he doesn't know is borrowed.

chapters.title: For Sale: Charming Safe House
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She finds the real estate listing on a routine sweep—twelve photos of the safe house interior, including the hidden server closet, staged like a lifestyle magazine shoot. The listing agent's phone number routes to a dead exchange in Prague. The beat: dread arriving politely, dressed as customer service.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours of Prague
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They run, but the extraction contact in Prague is dead when they arrive, arranged neatly to look like a heart attack. Dominic realizes the leak isn't sloppy—it's surgical, someone with full program access. First glimpse of Vesper's signature: a single white flower left on the body. The beat: the world tilting from job to hunt.

chapters.title: What Mara Knows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback-woven. She reveals the encrypted drive's contents: the Meridian Program brokers state-sanctioned killings through three governments' deniable channels, and her brother was one of its targets. She didn't flee to survive; she fled to testify. The beat: intimacy forged under threat—Dominic falling for her even as duty says deliver her back.

chapters.title: The Handler's Offer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His handler, Corliss, reaches out with a deal: hand over Mara and the drive, walk away rich and clean. Dominic stalls, lying fluently for the first time to his own side. Meanwhile Vesper makes contact—not attacking, but watching, leaving another white flower on his rental car. The beat: the polished lie beginning to crack against what he wants.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A brutal overland crossing through the Alps into Italy, bribing a trucker, nearly caught at a checkpoint when Mara's forged papers fail. Dominic improvises, burning his own identity documents to get them both through—one-way, no return. The beat: commitment made physical; there is no version of him that goes back now.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, first time. We learn the assassin was trained alongside Dominic years ago, that they were lovers before the program split them, and that the white flowers were always a signal between them: I see you, I choose not to kill you yet. Vesper reports false progress to Corliss while closing in for reasons even she can't name. The beat: the hunter revealed as haunted.

chapters.title: Rome, Burning Slowly
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hiding in Rome, they attempt to pass the drive to a journalist, but the meeting is compromised—Corliss anticipated it, and the journalist is taken. Dominic confesses his handler's offer; Mara forgives him not because he lied but because he chose her anyway. The beat: love fully admitted at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cornered in a Trastevere safe flat, Dominic faces Vesper alone and offers her the truth instead of a fight: the program will erase her too once this ends. Corliss arrives with a kill team, forcing all three onto the same side of the gun. The climax erupts—Corliss dies by his own protocol, and Vesper stands over Dominic, weapon raised. The beat: everything converging on a trigger.

chapters.title: Published
chapters.summary: Three POVs converge. Vesper lowers the gun and walks into the crowd, leaving a final white flower. Dominic and Mara release the Meridian files publicly from a Naples internet café, then scatter his go-bag's contents into the harbor—no bag, no lie, no border left to guard. Epilogue beat: months later, anonymous, they watch the fallout on a stranger's television, free and unimportant at last.
